identity.industry: Indian Alcobev / Premium & Above IMFL Consolidation

summary.oneLiner: Tilaknagar reported a transformative Q4FY26 with 135% volume growth driven by the first full quarter of Imperial Blue, though reported revenue margins compressed due to a strategic accounting change netting selling expenses against revenue. The core thesis hinges on successful integration (75% TSMA exit achieved), targeting 16-18% EBITDA margins via synergies and cost optimization, while guiding net debt/EBITDA below 1.0x by FY29.

one-line thesis: Tilaknagar reported a transformative Q4FY26 with 135% volume growth driven by the first full quarter of Imperial Blue, though reported revenue margins compressed due to a strategic accounting change netting selling expenses against revenue. The core thesis hinges on successful integration (75% TSMA exit achieved), targeting 16-18% EBITDA margins via synergies and cost optimization, while guiding net debt/EBITDA below 1.0x by FY29.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 949 Cr (+148% YoY, impacted by new accounting netting selling expenses); EBITDA: INR 155 Cr (+97% YoY), Margin 16.3% (15.5% adj. for subsidy); PAT: Impacted by INR 63 Cr exceptional expense (TSMA fees/labor code); Order Book: N/A (FMCG); Net Debt: INR 1,911 Cr (Gross Debt INR 2,295 Cr). One-offs: INR 63 Cr exceptional charge in Q4; Accounting distortion: Selling expenses now deducted from Gross Revenue, lowering top-line and gross margin but inflating EBITDA/PAT margins.
guidance: Volume Growth: High-single to low-double digit for FY27, double-digit CAGR over 3 years; Margin: 16%-18% EBITDA over 24-36 months; Order Inflow: N/A; Capex: Maintenance only (~INR 25 Cr/year for FY27-28).
order book & pipeline: Not applicable for FMCG/Alcobev sector; focus is on volume throughput and distribution reach.
segment / subsidiary detail: Imperial Blue contributed 4.6 Mn cases in Q4 (total 8 Mn+); Ex-IB volumes grew 14% in FY26 to 13.6 Mn cases; Mansion House crossed 10 Mn cases benchmark; IB seasonality is flatter than TI legacy (H2 ~52% of vol).
growth verticals / optionality: Pan-India expansion of legacy brands (Mansion House) into North/West markets in FY27; Luxury portfolio expansion via Spaceman Spirits Lab (Monarch, Amara Vodka); Nigeria subsidiary investment (INR 30 Cr) to capture 2.5 Lakh case opportunity.
margins & cost dynamics: Current Q4 margin 15.5% (adj); Path to 16-18% via: 60-100 bps from India-UK FTA (custom duty on Scotch); Supply chain synergies (bottling cost savings INR 10 Cr/yr from Prag expansion); Operating leverage; Potential price hikes in Telangana. Risks: Geopolitical input cost inflation.
capex / expansion: Prag (Andhra Pradesh) expansion completed (INR 59 Cr invested), capacity raised from 6 Lakh to 36 Lakh cases/annum; Future capex limited to maintenance (~INR 25 Cr/annum); Shrirampur ENA distillery recommissioning under consideration.
capital allocation: Priority on debt reduction (Net Debt/EBITDA <1.0x by FY29); Dividend recommended INR 1/share; Deferred consideration of EUR 28 Mn payable to Pernod Ricard after 4 years; Working capital cycle targeted at 53-55 days.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical tension driving raw material inflation; Delay in TSMA transition for remaining 3 states (target full exit by FY27 end); Regulatory uncertainty on excise policies (Telangana dues outstanding); Integration execution risk in non-southern markets.
management quality / tone: Confident and operationally focused; emphasized 'record volumes' post-TSMA exit disruptions; transparent on accounting changes; cautious on Q1 margin pressure due to inflation but firm on full-year guidance.
non-obvious takeaways: The accounting reclassification of selling expenses creates a false impression of margin expansion (EBITDA margin up) while actually compressing the top-line; the INR 63 Cr exceptional charge masks underlying operational profitability; TSMA fees will drop from ~INR 63 Cr (Q4 impact) to INR 55-60 Cr full year FY27 as transition completes.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Input cost inflation and integration friction | United Spirits Ltd | beneficiary | Med | If TI faces margin pressure from inflation or integration delays, market share gains in premium whiskey could flow to the category leader. |
| Price wars in Southern India | Radico Khaitan Ltd | loser | Low | TI's aggressive volume growth and price cuts in Karnataka/AP could pressure competitors' pricing power in the P&A segment. |

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- 'Largest domestic Prestige & Above (P&A) IMFL player and third-largest P&A IMFL player in India'; also 'Largest P&A IMFL Player in South-India'.
- 'Largest P&A player in South India with ~40% market share (ex-Tamil Nadu)'.
- Brand claims stated verbatim: 'Mansion House is the highest selling & fastest growing premium brandy in the World' and 'Imperial Blue is the 3rd largest whisky Globally' (source: 'Media Reports, Management Estimates'). The accompanying badge grid of ordinals (1st/2nd/3rd/7th/8th) loses its label-to-value binding in extraction, so the individual rankings are not asserted here.
- 'Highest Selling Deluxe Whisky in Jun-26' is claimed for the portfolio in the Q1 FY27 header strip.
- Two years ago the company describes itself as a '2-brand and 1-category player' with '90%+ volume saliency from Brandy' and '85%+ volume saliency from Southern India'; the stated journey ahead is a 'Pan-India Player with 2 of the largest brands in 2 of the largest IMFL Categories' with '65%+ and 30%+ volume saliency from Whisky and Brandy respectively' (data for LTM Mar-26).

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Imperial Blue was acquired from a third party with the acquisition 'completed in Nov-25' (hence YoY growth 'not applicable' for IB); integration is 'substantially completed' with one state left under the Transition Services and Manufacturing Agreement (TSMA), max exit Q4 FY27.
- [Regulation] 'The India-UK Free Trade Agreement came into effect in mid-July' with reduced Scotch import costs expected in financials from Q3 FY27; 'Karnataka – one of the largest markets for both IB and MHB, is witnessing strong growth on the back of the recent excise policy reforms'.
- [Accounting change] From Q4 FY26 onwards selling expenses (discounts, schemes and similar incentives) move from Other Expense to a reduction from Gross Revenue; the deck's illustration shows GP margin falling from 50% to 44% and EBITDA margin rising from 15% to 17% with 'No Change' to EBITDA — made because the business expanded into non-corporation market states after the IB acquisition.
- [Associate/Investee] Spaceman Spirits Lab (SSL) 'clocks 2.2x volume over Q1 FY26'; SSL brands are being launched in TI strongholds under a 'Usership Agreement' across Southern, Northern, Eastern and North-Eastern markets over FY27.
- [Brand marketing] New Imperial Blue theme communication rolled out across 'nearly 28,000 on-trade and off-trade outlets nationwide', with long-term tie-ups signed with 82.5 Grey, Essence Media, Dentsu Isobar and Apostrophe.
